acceptance_signals: Every current public page reachable from the homepage, portfolio, quickstarts, interview guides, replay contract, and Harness contract uses consistent branded navigation, readable styling, and a valid favicon.
Affected current pages state the stable 0.2.1, published 0.3.0rc1, and development-source boundaries consistently without rewriting historical release facts.
Deterministic tests crawl the published document graph and reject internal 404s, unresolved templates, missing shared assets, or broken bilingual navigation.
Distinct desktop and narrow-width checks cover each public page template, and the full supported test suite passes before completion.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-cbfdc577c554439a8593cf0882f18b82 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control. The aligned complete public Pages journey synchronization, deterministic and visual validation, native current-Agent self-review, and documentation closeout completed; the bounded local task is now paused without Git, publication, release, deployment, historical-rewrite, generated-report-rewrite, or follow-on authority.

requirement.summary: Apply one coherent branded shell, navigation, favicon, release-boundary presentation, and deterministic internal-resource protection to every current GitHub Pages surface reachable through the interview and adoption journey, while preserving current product behavior and historical evidence.

items: A shared Jekyll layout could unintentionally restyle historical documents outside the current public journey.
Repository Pages base-path handling could break root-relative links.
Static HTML and Markdown-generated pages can drift unless tests cover both render paths.
Publication, Git operations, release, and deployment are outside this task and require separate human authorization.
Reviewed assumption: GitHub Pages continues to build the docs directory with Jekyll for Markdown-backed pages.
Reviewed assumption: The current standalone page visual identity is the shared baseline.
Reviewed assumption: Generated sample-report bytes and historical ADR, release, experiment, and dated-log facts remain unchanged.
Reviewed unknown: The exact minimal layout and asset set will be confirmed by repository inspection.
